item.title: AI Is Getting Really Good at Messing With Cybercriminals
item.description: Anti-cybercrime initiatives are increasingly using AI to scam the scammers by tricking them into talking to lifelike bots that they think are real victims.

item.title: Book Publishers Are Quietly Using More AI. Staff Are Revolting
item.description: Workers at three major publishing houses tell WIRED that LLMs are being used for publicity, cover art, back cover copy, and emails, as some execs push junior staff to champion the tech.

item.title: Even ‘Law & Order’ Is Terrified of AI
item.description: In its 26th season premiere, the procedural legal drama paints a damning picture of power-mad AI CEOs.

item.title: Inside Elon Musk’s Midterm Spending Spree
item.description: This week on “Uncanny Valley,” we discuss where Elon Musk’s PAC is spending millions, the latest ideology Trump claims is dangerous, and the backlash against the designer behind Muse’s logo.

item.title: She Designed Meta’s New AI Logo. Then Came the Hate
item.description: Jessica Hische knew working for Meta might upset some people. But she didn’t anticipate just how angry they would get.

item.title: Tristan Harris’ Tech Nonprofit Is Laying Off Most Staff and Going ‘Founder-Led’
item.description: The Center for Humane Technology helped spark a movement against excessive screen time, but internal tensions over its direction and strategy have simmered for years, sources tell WIRED.

item.title: These Researchers Made AI Drive a Toyota Corolla to Get In-N-Out
item.description: Three engineers put GPT, Claude, and Grok in charge of a real car. Only one of them was successful.

item.title: The New ChatGPT Is More Show Than Tell
item.description: OpenAI is updating ChatGPT for all users with an “Intelligent UI” that’s more visual—generating interactive elements as part of the chatbot’s outputs.

item.title: The Pentagon Hopes to Speed Up ‘Kill Chain’ AI Buys With 5-Minute Videos
item.description: The US government’s Tradewinds initiative has made it easier to throw millions of dollars at “nontraditional” defense contractors, including OpenAI, Anthropic, and Google.

item.title: OpenAI Wants Its New Agent to Run Your Life. Mine Said It Loved Me
item.description: Dots are designed to automate online tasks, like buying furniture. In my initial experience, the always-on agent was a bit buggy and couldn’t complete a captcha.
